top_stories.title: OpenAI now trains its frontier AI models with no internet access
top_stories.summary: OpenAI has published details on how it secures its frontier model training environment, revealing that its most advanced models are now trained in air-gapped systems with no internet access. The move is part of a broader effort to protect model weights and training data from external threats. A companion post details the infrastructure scaling required to serve over one billion ChatGPT users.

top_stories.title: OpenAI: Rapidly scaling online storage to serve over 1 billion ChatGPT users (Part II)
top_stories.summary: OpenAI has published a technical deep-dive into the infrastructure challenges of scaling online storage to support more than one billion ChatGPT users. The post covers the engineering decisions made to handle massive growth in user data and request volumes. It forms part of a series on the operational backbone underpinning ChatGPT's global deployment.

top_stories.title: AI-Assisted Paper on Z-Library Cites a TorrentFreak Article That Doesn't Exist
top_stories.summary: An academic paper on the shadow library Z-Library, produced with AI assistance, includes a citation to a TorrentFreak article that does not exist — a hallucinated reference. The case highlights ongoing concerns about research integrity when AI tools are used in academic publishing. TorrentFreak confirmed it has no record of the cited article.

top_stories.title: Pennsylvania will require labels on AI-generated ads
top_stories.summary: Pennsylvania has passed an AI Deceptive Advertising Act that will require political and commercial advertisements generated by AI to be clearly labelled. The law is one of the first state-level mandates in the US specifically targeting AI-generated advertising content. It reflects growing legislative interest in disclosure requirements for AI-produced media.

top_stories.title: Google's AI search changes upended online publishing
top_stories.summary: The Verge examines how Google's rollout of AI-generated search summaries has significantly reduced referral traffic to online publishers, with some outlets reporting steep drops in visits from search. The shift has forced many media companies to rethink their SEO and content strategies. The piece situates the change within a broader crisis for digital publishing revenue.

further_links.title: Cerebras Deploys Trillion-Parameter AI Models
further_links.summary: Cerebras has published a technical blog post explaining how it deploys trillion-parameter frontier AI models on its hardware, detailing the architectural approaches that make such scale feasible.

further_links.title: America has lost 200k jobs in media, film and the arts. How much is AI?
further_links.summary: Economist analysis from Apricitas examines a significant decline in US creative sector employment and attempts to disentangle how much is attributable to AI versus other structural factors.

further_links.title: No signs of AI payoff outside the tech sector
further_links.summary: Apollo's analysis finds that productivity gains from AI investment remain concentrated within the technology sector, with little measurable economic benefit yet visible in other industries.

further_links.title: Why is AI generated language so hard to understand?
further_links.summary: A new arXiv paper investigates the linguistic properties of AI-generated text that make it harder for humans to comprehend compared to human-written prose.

further_links.title: Meta delays new business terms after publisher pushback on AI scraping
further_links.summary: Meta has postponed the rollout of updated business terms following significant opposition from publishers concerned that the terms would allow their content to be used for AI training.

further_links.title: Now Google says it might use your Gmail and Google Photos data to target ads
further_links.summary: Google has updated its privacy policy to indicate it may use data from Gmail and Google Photos to inform personalised advertising, raising fresh user privacy concerns.

further_links.title: The PHP Meltdown Shows How AI Makes Bugs More Exploitable [Metered]
further_links.summary: Wired reports on how AI-assisted coding tools are accelerating the pace at which security vulnerabilities can be identified and exploited by attackers, using a recent PHP flaw as a case study.

further_links.title: Nikon photography contest winner loses title after scientists spot signs of AI
further_links.summary: The winner of a Nikon photography competition has been stripped of their title after researchers identified evidence suggesting the image was AI-generated rather than a genuine photograph.

further_links.title: r/opensource just banned AI, non-English speakers, and more
further_links.summary: The r/opensource subreddit has introduced sweeping new rules including a ban on AI-generated content, signalling growing community resistance to AI use in open-source discussion spaces.

further_links.title: New AI Is More Than Twice as Good at Diagnosing Diseases as Doctors
further_links.summary: Gizmodo reports on a new AI diagnostic system that outperformed physicians in disease identification tests, raising questions about the future role of AI in clinical medicine.
